title: Upsell Sequence CSA Toolkit
content:
Purpose: Practical, reusable CSA toolkit for sequencing expansion conversations (Dedicated capacity, Private deployment pilots, premium SLA bundles). This doc is a living draft: pick the fragments you need, copy into your QBR, and update signals/attachments per account.

High-level approach (one-liner): Diagnose value + technical readiness, stage offers to reduce risk, and align economics to customer business milestones.

Quick checklist (first 30 days with an eligible account):
- Confirm contract end dates and auto-renew windows (Jira check: JIRA-4567).
- Surface usage patterns: median latency, peak tokens/day, tail-rate percentiles (ask infra/telemetry owner for last 90d).
- Identify 1–2 internal champions and 1 partner stakeholder (security/compliance/infra).
- Classify customer into a risk tier (A/B/C) for cadence and discount bands.
- Technical readiness baseline: API connectivity, model pinning, key management, network egress rules.

Signals that warrant expansion outreach:
- Sustained 30%+ month-over-month token growth for 3 months.
- Repeated tail-latency breaches > target SLA or recurring throttles.
- Evaluations showing quality regression on smaller models and interest in private model hosting.
- Compliance/regulatory trigger: customer requests VPC or audit logs.

QBR agenda snippet (10–15 minutes reserved for expansion conversation):
1) Current-state summary (owner: CSA) — usage, cost drivers, incidents in last quarter.
2) Business impact metric (customer input) — where LLM saves time or increases revenue.
3) Gap & proposal — proposed Dedicated/Private/SLA bundle and expected delta in latency/cost/visibility.
4) Risks & mitigations — security review timeline, infra work, migration sprint.
5) Next steps & decision window — sample dates for pilot start, procurement sign-off.

Sample QBR talking points (short bullets for slide speaker notes):
- "You’re consuming ~2M tokens/day with pronounced peak windows; our Dedicated pools reduce tail latency and provide consistent throughput for those spikes."
- "Private deployment will remove egress constraints and give you VM-level isolation; proposed approach is a 4–6 week pilot with customer-managed VPC and limited read-only logs."
- "Premium SLA adds 99.95% uptime and a 30-minute on-call response for P1s — we’ll scope runbook integration during the pilot."

Offer sequencing patterns (play types):
- Low-friction: Premium SLA add-on on top of hosted API. Pricing: fixed monthly fee + small per-token uplift. Best when customer needs predictable SLOs but not full isolation.
- Medium-friction: Dedicated reservation. Pricing: committed monthly GPU hours + overage. Best when throughput and cost predictability are top priorities.
- High-friction: Private deployment (VPC or on-prem). Pricing: platform license + deployment labor + managed services. Best when audit/compliance or data residency is required.

Recommended sequencing example (for mid-market account):
Week 0: QBR introduces SLA add-on (pilot window + pricing).
Week 2: Technical discovery for Dedicated feasibility (workload profile, kernel/quantization needs).
Week 4: SLA pilot live on current tenancy; measure latency and incident response.
Week 8: If SLA pilot successful, propose Dedicated reservation with 3-month runway.
Week 12–20: If regulatory requirements surface, propose Private deployment timeline.

Negotiation playbook (discount calculus & concessions):
- Always anchor to value: show end-to-end savings (token-level cost reduction for Dedicated, ops+compliance risk reduction for Private).
- Offer time-boxed pilots: 3-month pilot with no long-term commitment reduces procurement friction.
- Use tiered discounts: larger committed spend -> higher discount + faster provisioning SLA.
- Preserve price integrity: keep platform-fee and managed-service pricing distinct from token/compute pricing to avoid margin leakage.

Technical readiness checklist (copyable into tech discovery form):
- API key lifecycle: rotation policy, existing secrets in KMS?
- Network: IP allowlist, VPC peering, egress bandwidth caps.
- Model artifacts: do they require private model uploads, or can we serve via Redwood catalog?
- Data residency: filters, redaction, and audit log retention.
- Integration points: tracing hooks, cost-level tokens, rollout policies.

Risk matrix (short):
- Risk: Procurement delay -> Mitigation: Offer pilot SOW and short trial contract.
- Risk: Security review fails -> Mitigation: provide Security-Reviewed Architecture Packet; offer ephemeral private enclave.
- Risk: Performance mismatch -> Mitigation: propose Dedicated baseline + burst capacity and rollback policy.

Renewal & tracking template (rows for spreadsheet copy):
Columns (as a single-line CSV): account_name,renewal_date,current_mrr,usage_last_90d,primary_champion,tech_readiness,recommended_offer,proposal_date,decision_by,probability,notes
Example row:
"Acme Retail,2026-03-30,8500,3.2M tokens/day,Alex Rivera,green,Dedicated-3mo-pilot,2026-01-15,2026-02-28,0.7,security review pending"

Email templates (short, editable):
- Intro + pilot ask:
Subject: Proposal to pilot premium SLA for [Customer]
Hi [Champion],
We’ve observed peak latency during holiday windows that impact X customer flows. We’d like to propose a short pilot of our premium SLA (no infra changes) to validate reduced incident impact and a measured ROI. Pilot terms: 6 weeks, billing at +X/month, opt-out after pilot. Can we schedule 30m to walk the scope?
Thanks,
[CSA name]

- Follow-up after technical discovery:
Subject: Technical next steps for Dedicated evaluation
Hi [Infra contact],
Thanks for the discovery. Attached is the migration checklist and a 4-week timeline for a Dedicated pilot. We’ll need a list of IPs for routing and an internal contact for VPN/VPC setup.
Best,
[Solutions Engineer name]

Internal playbook snippets for CSA/SE collaboration (short):
- When to escalate to SE: any request for private model hosting, custom quantization, or unsupported architectural changes.
- When to involve Legal: reseller/third-party data routing or export controls.
- SRE touchpoints: pre-provision capacity and run load test script (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/load-tests).

KPIs & success criteria (proposal):
- SLA add-on: reduce P95 latency by 20% and decrease incident MTTR by 40% in pilot window.
- Dedicated: reduce token unit cost by >=15% at current commit and keep tail latency within target.
- Private: complete deployment within agreed window and pass SOC-2 like checklist.

Playbook maintenance notes (how to keep this doc fresh):
- Owner: Priya Kannan (update quarterly).
- Pull telemetry examples quarterly from telemetry:dashboard:account-usage.
- Log any successful upsell and anonymized metrics to Confluence case studies page (linked_artifacts above).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add sample SOW template for 3-month Dedicated pilot.
- Add anonymized case study for mid-market to show math.
- Add formal cost calc sheet and copy to product-hosted-api/monetization templates.

End of doc.
